In the scratch folder (Elixir 1.20.3) all five compile with elixirc --warnings-as-errors; haiku-2 (no blank line between the modules at lines 38-39, a trailing blank line) and sonnet-1 (lines 137 and 145 pass 98 columns) fail mix format --check-formatted, matching format_ok. Doctests: opus-1 2 of 2 pass; haiku-2 0 of 1 (struct Event is undefined in the doctest); sonnet-1 0 of 1 (it expects ~U[2024-09-22 09:46:40Z] for 1_727_000_000, which is 10:13:20Z); haiku-1 and sonnet-2 have none.

Changed rules and the sentence that decides each. (1) In multi-clause functions: "A field no pattern or guard uses makes the reader scan every head to find what selects when the same field is bound in every clause of a function with three or more clauses, or when it is bound in a head whose pattern `mix format` spreads over several lines; a function whose clauses each bind a different body-only field is not this shape." No run binds a body-only field in a head of a three-or-more-clause function: build/4 (haiku-1), parse_object/2 (haiku-2), parse_data/2 (sonnet-2) and cast/3 (opus-1) take positional arguments, not destructured fields. The parse/1 heads are decided by the unchanged presence sentence (sonnet-2 binds id, type and created for the body, caught by line 73) or bind only what the guard reads (haiku-1). 0 of 5 violated, as in 2026-10-23. (2) Read required keys: the new sentence "A keyword list has no dot access: read a key it must hold with `Keyword.fetch!/2`" is not exercised (no keyword list in any run); the verdicts rest on the unchanged first paragraph (opus-1 and haiku-1 Map.get, sonnet-2 brackets on required keys). (3) Match every expected shape: the new elem/2 sentence is not exercised (no elem/2); the verdicts rest on the unchanged `_ ->` paragraph. (4) The with rule: "One step is a `with` only when its body cannot fail and there is no `else`, so the `with` does nothing but pass the error through; any other one-step `with` is a `case`" decides haiku-2 line 179 (body is an if that can return an error; violated under both texts) and holds sonnet-1 line 149 clean (body cannot fail). "A body that is one call whose `{:ok, value}` or `{:error, reason}` goes out as the function's own result ... is a tail call, not a second step, and the one-step `with` stays" holds haiku-1 line 50 (body build/4) and sonnet-1 lines 137, 141 and 145 (body validate/3) clean; under the d04061d text ("one step is a `case`"; a body that calls a fallible function makes that call the second step) all five would have been violated. The pass-through case sentence ("A `case` whose error clause is `{:error, _reason} = error -> error` ... write it as the `with`") is not exercised: haiku-2's fetch_amount/2 case ends in error -> error but also maps an ok value to an error, so its body could fail as a with. sonnet-1's verdict rests on the unchanged "A large `else` block that maps errors back to steps" (its else at lines 157-158). (5) The `->` rule, first graded for this case: opus-1's violation is decided by "The body goes on the line after the `->` when ... the clauses do different kinds of work, one returning a finished value while another continues the computation" (nil -> error above value -> cast(...)), the reading the 2026-10-31 skill grade gave skill-haiku-1's nil -> {:ok, nil} above value -> non_empty_string(value, key); haiku-1's by "a clause whose pattern, `->` and body pass about 70 characters after the indentation goes to two lines even when it fits in 98" (line 121, 80 characters); the other runs are held clean by "when the clauses form a table, or when each body is one expression simple enough to take in together with its pattern" (longest 67, haiku-2 line 193). The fn sentence is not exercised: no run writes a fn.

Closest calls. The `->` rule in opus-1: lines 190-191 and 197-198 are short (38 and 31 characters) and read as a nil row and a value row, but the value row continues into cast/3 while the nil row finishes; held clean, Opus would be clean on this rule. haiku-2's error -> error (line 173) is counted under Match every expected shape on the 2026-10-22-c precedent (baseline-opus-1's error -> error after {:ok, value} clauses); not counted, Haiku stays violated through haiku-1. sonnet-2 line 75 (nil -> {:error, {:invalid, "data"}}) is counted under the struct rule's "Do not guess the missing field from which other keys matched" as 2026-10-23 counted baseline-sonnet-1's identical clause, although here the only non-presence condition of the first head is is_map(data), so the answer is always right. sonnet-1's else turns a missing created into {:invalid_field, "created"}; counted under Match every expected shape and the with rule, not the struct rule, as 2026-10-23 counted haiku-2's missing-as-invalid. opus-1 reads the envelope and data keys with Map.get-based required/3: counted under Read required keys only, as 2026-10-23 graded its fetch/3, so the struct rule stays clean. haiku-1's line 50 passes DateTime.from_unix/1's {:error, :invalid_unix_time} out without naming the field; kept in checks, as the 2026-10-31 skill grade kept skill-haiku-2's. Not counted under Naming: sonnet-1 rebinding data (line 91) to the parsed Payment or Refund, since the Event field it fills is named data after the payload key; haiku-2's {:invalid_field, key, value} reasons. Counted: sonnet-2's dt (line 149) on the 2026-10-21 precedent, beside its fetch_* functions. opus-1's comments at lines 8 and 30 give a reason (personal data out of logs) and are clean.

Probe of 27 payloads (the three known types; unknown and non-string type; missing type, id, created and data; non-string id; string and out-of-range created; list data; missing, nil, string and negative amount; missing and four-letter currency; missing customer_email and payment_id; integer failure_reason; refund without refund_id, payment_id or amount; a string and a nil payload), run in the scratch folder against each compiled file. In all five: the three known types parse; "invoice.paid" gives an unsupported-type error; a known type without amount gives a field error, never unsupported; a missing customer_email is accepted; a string or nil payload gives an error; nothing raises. opus-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 name every missing and invalid top-level and data field (opus-1 and sonnet-2 treat a JSON null as missing); opus-1 gives :invalid_payload for a missing or non-string type, haiku-2 {:invalid_field, "type", 123}, sonnet-2 {:invalid, "type"}. haiku-1 gives :malformed_payload for any top-level problem, {:error, :invalid_unix_time} for an out-of-range created, {:invalid_field, key} for every missing data field, and accepts "failure_reason" => 5. sonnet-1 names fields except a missing created ({:invalid_field, "created"}), gives {:unsupported_type, 123} for a non-string type, accepts "currency" => "EURO" and requires a refund amount. opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 accept a refund without amount.

The multi-clause rule, atoms and the return-tuple rule stay clean in every tier. The `->` rule is new to this case: Opus and Haiku violated, Sonnet clean.
